correctness.rationale: Rescaling by the axes identifies the normalized law with a signed Dirichlet vector with d unit parameters and slack alpha+1. Each coordinate magnitude T is Beta(1,m), with second moment 2/((m+1)(m+2)); sign symmetry diagonalizes the Gram matrix. The resulting row 1+c sum_i x_i y_i/a_i² uses c=(m+1)(m+2)/2>1. The row mass is convex, and distinct vertex rows have opposite signs on positive-measure interior sets close to the negative of a vertex, so equality is possible only at a vertex. At a vertex the excess over 1 equals E(cT−1)_+ = c integral_[1/c,1] (1−t)^m dt, giving the formula. The sign row and negative-set indicator yield the two claimed extremal values by unit row mass, and self-adjointness gives L1 duality. Full support and affine continuity justify vertex values for essential suprema. For excess F and b=1−2/((m+1)(m+2)), differentiation and log b>−(1−b)/b give (log F)'>(m²+5m+2)/(m(m+2)(m+3))>0. Expansion b^m=1−2/m+8/m²+O(m^-3) gives the stated norm; E(sum |Y_i|/a_i)=d/(m+1) proves weak concentration at fixed d. This includes d=1 and all m>d−1 in fixed d. Replay: RESULT.md lines 25–58.
